failures.title: BMW S68B44 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Cooling System Complexity - multiple circuits and electric water pumps
items.onset: Unknown (engine is relatively new; early data limited)
items.whatHappens: The S68B44 features a split cooling system with separate circuits for the engine, turbos, and hybrid components, plus electric water pumps. Early forum reports indicate potential for leaks at plastic connections and pump failures, though long‑term data is not yet available.
items.repairVsReplace: Cooling system components are individually replaceable, but access is difficult. Preventative inspection at 40k miles is recommended.

items.title: Oil Pump Chain Tensioner - potential fatigue
items.whatHappens: The S68B44 carries forward some design elements from the S63, including a chain‑driven oil pump. The tensioner may wear over time, causing oil pressure drops. This is speculative at this stage - the S68 has revised components, but owners should monitor oil pressure and engine noise.
items.repairVsReplace: If oil pressure drops, immediate investigation is required. Tensioner replacement is a standalone repair if caught early; failure can lead to bottom‑end damage.

failures.goodYearsLine: The S68B44 is too new to have a well‑established failure profile. Early indicators suggest it is more robust than the S63 family, with the 48V system adding complexity but also enabling higher efficiency. All production years are similar; 2024+ models may have small revisions.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the S68B44
variants.intro: The S68B44 is BMW's latest high‑performance V8, introduced in 2022. It is the first M V8 to feature a 48V mild‑hybrid integrated starter‑generator (ISG) located between the engine and transmission, enabling additional torque and smoother start‑stop. Where to find the engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped plate near the left bank (viewed from the driver's seat) - On the V5C registration document - under engine number - Via a BMW VIN decoder - the 7th and 8th characters of the VIN identify the engine family Commonly confused codes: - S63B44T4 - the previous M V8, without mild‑hybrid and with older fuel/ignition systems; not interchangeable - S63TU - the S63 family page; some older XM prototypes may have used S63 variants, but production XMs use S68 - N63B44B - the non‑M version of the N63 V8, not to be confused with S68

relatives.description: the final evolution of BMW's previous M V8, found in the F90 M5 CS and later M8 variants. The S63T4 produced up to 635 hp but lacked the S68's 48V mild‑hybrid system; the S68's integrated starter‑generator and revised hot‑vee design represent a significant step forward in both power delivery and efficiency. [S63B44T4 Engine - /bmw/s63b44t4-engine/]

the family page covering the entire S63 generation (T0-T4). The S68 is not part of the S63 family - it's a new engine with a different architecture and hybrid integration - but the S63TU page is useful for understanding the lineage. [S63TU Engine - /bmw/s63tu-engine/]

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement S68B44 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used S68B44 is only viable if you can obtain a complete unit with its hybrid components (ISG, wiring, cooling) from a low‑mileage, accident‑damaged car. Given the engine's recent introduction, used units are extremely rare and command high prices (£8,000-£12,000). Verify that the 48V system and all sensors are included - missing components will be costly to source. Used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A reconditioned S68B44 is the most practical choice for owners of XM or new M5 models, provided the specialist has access to BMW's latest diagnostic tools and software. A proper recon will include new timing chain components, cooling system refresh, and hybrid system calibration. Expect £12,000-£18,000 with 12-24 months warranty - but availability is currently limited. Reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full S68B44 rebuild is a specialist undertaking due to the hybrid system. This is only justified for extreme high‑performance builds or warranty replacement. Costs are likely to exceed £16,000-£22,000. As of 2025, very few UK workshops have experience rebuilding this engine. Rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Our vetted UK BMW M specialists are now gaining experience with the S68 platform - supply‑only or full supply‑and‑fit available, with warranty on reconditioned units. Supply and fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The S68B44 sits in cars worth £80,000-£200,000+ (XM, new M5). A reconditioned S68B44 at £12,000-£18,000 represents 10‑20% of vehicle value - well within safe territory. However, because the engine is so new, replacement parts and expertise are scarce, which may inflate actual costs. Consider the overall availability of specialist support before committing.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the S68B44 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The S68B44 is too new to have a well‑established failure profile. Early reports indicate potential cooling system complexity and oil pump chain tensioner wear, but long‑term data is not yet available. The split cooling system with electric pumps is a new design. mainEntity.name: Which BMW M models have the S68B44 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The S68B44 powers the BMW XM (G09), new G90 M5, G99 M5 Touring, and will power future X5 M and X6 M variants from 2025 onwards. It replaced the S63 family from 2022. The 48V mild‑hybrid system is integrated between the engine and transmission.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned S68B44?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned S68B44 is the safer choice, provided the specialist has BMW's latest diagnostic tools and experience with the hybrid system. Used units are scarce and may lack hybrid components. Reconditioning addresses the engine's internal wear while preserving the hybrid calibration. For XM owners, reconditioned is the only practical option.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my car has the S68B44 and not another V8 variant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The engine code is stamped on the block (left bank) and listed on your V5C or via a BMW VIN decoder. It is commonly confused with S63B44T4 and older S63 variants. The presence of 48V hybrid system and the G09/G90 chassis codes confirm S68. Fitting a non‑hybrid S63 engine will not work - the hybrid system is integrated.

mainEntity.name: Is the S68B44 a reliable engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The S68B44 is too new to have a definitive reliability reputation - early data suggests it is BMW's most advanced V8, but complexity is high. The 48V mild‑hybrid system adds components that may require maintenance. The hot‑vee cooling and turbo setup is similar to S63, but revised. Expect higher ownership costs due to specialist parts and labour.
